title: Hannibal Barca
summary: Hannibal Barca was a Carthaginian general of the Second Punic War (218–202 BCE). He led an army with war elephants across the Pyrenees and Alps into Italy and defeated Roman armies at the Trebia, Lake Trasimene and Cannae, before Scipio Africanus defeated him at Zama in 202 BCE.

uncertainty.note: Born 247 BCE in Carthage; died in exile at Libyssa (Bithynia) c. 183–182 BCE.

as_recorded.value: The Carthaginian general Hannibal (247-182 BCE) was one of the greatest military leaders in history.
Hannibal (also known as Hannibal Barca, l. 247-183 BCE) was a Carthaginian general during the Second Punic War between Carthage and Rome (218-202 BCE).
When Hannibal (in his own, Punic language: Hanba'al , "mercy of Ba'al ") was born in 247 BCE, his birthplace Carthage was about to lose a long and important war.

where.modern_name: Carthage, Tunis Governorate, Tunisia (birthplace and capital; military campaigns traversed Spain, the Alps, Italy, and North Africa)
where.historical_name: Qart-ḥadašt (Carthago), capital of the Carthaginian Empire

importance.justification: Carthage's premier military commander whose invasion of Italy posed the greatest external crisis the Roman Republic ever faced.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the exact Alpine mountain pass crossed by Hannibal in 218 BCE, which remains an unsettled controversy among modern topographers and geomorphologists.
